cls: Vinca alkaloid antineoplastic - mitotic spindle (microtubule) inhibitor
quick: Initial 3.7 mg/m2 IV weekly, titrated by WBC (regimen-specific)
Contraindicated - can cause fetal harm (avoid; use contraception)
Reduce dose with hepatic impairment / high bilirubin
Not relevant to administration; avoid hepatotoxins
CBC (nadir), injection site, neuro exam, liver function
summary: Vinblastine sulfate is a vinca-alkaloid chemotherapy agent that binds tubulin and arrests cells in metaphase. It is used in Hodgkin and non-Hodgkin lymphoma, testicular germ-cell tumours, Kaposi sarcoma and other malignancies, often in combination regimens (e.g., ABVD). It MUST be given intravenously ONLY - intrathecal administration is uniformly FATAL. Dose-limiting myelosuppression (especially leukopenia) is its principal toxicity, and it is a potent vesicant that causes severe tissue injury on extravasation.
indications: Hodgkin lymphoma (e.g., as part of ABVD)
Advanced breast cancer unresponsive to other therapy

dosage.n: First dose; subsequent doses titrated to WBC response

dosage.d: Increase stepwise to 5.5, 7.4, 9.25, up to 18.5 mg/m2 IV
dosage.n: Increase only if WBC has recovered; do not exceed dose that drops WBC to ~3000/mm3
Titrated upward by similar percentage steps to max 12.5 mg/m2
Vinblastine is hepatically cleared; reduce in cholestasis

admin: FOR INTRAVENOUS USE ONLY - FATAL if given by any other route, especially intrathecal
Dispense in a syringe labelled: 'For IV use only - fatal if given by other routes'
Administer as a slow IV injection or into the tubing of a running IV infusion over about 1 minute
Vesicant - avoid extravasation; if it occurs, stop, aspirate, and apply local heat with hyaluronidase per protocol
Flush the vein/line after administration; confirm needle is in the vein before injecting
moa: Vinblastine binds to tubulin dimers, inhibiting microtubule assembly and disrupting the mitotic spindle. This arrests dividing cells in metaphase (M phase), leading to cell-cycle blockade and apoptosis. At higher concentrations it also interferes with other microtubule-dependent processes such as cellular metabolism and transport.

absolute: Significant granulocytopenia not related to the disease being treated
monitor: Neurologic status (less neurotoxic than vincristine but possible)

preg: Contraindicated in pregnancy. Vinblastine is teratogenic and embryotoxic in animals and can cause fetal harm. Women of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during and after treatment, and men should be advised regarding potential infertility.
lact: Contraindicated during breastfeeding. It is not known whether vinblastine is excreted in human milk; because of the potential for serious adverse effects in the infant, discontinue nursing during therapy.
renal: No specific renal dose adjustment is established. Use with caution; ensure adequate hydration to manage hyperuricemia from tumour lysis.
hepatic: Vinblastine is metabolized by the liver and excreted in bile. Dose reduction is required in hepatic impairment or biliary obstruction; commonly the dose is reduced by 50% when serum bilirubin is 1.5-3 mg/dL and the drug is withheld at higher levels.

major: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors e.g. azole antifungals, erythromycin, ritonavir (increased vinblastine toxicity)
Other myelosuppressive chemotherapy/radiation (additive bone marrow suppression)
moderate: Phenytoin (vinblastine may reduce phenytoin absorption/levels - monitor)
Live vaccines (risk of disseminated infection in immunosuppressed patients)
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor uric acid (tumour lysis); CBC for nadir

serious: Severe myelosuppression with neutropenia and infection
emergency: FATAL ascending neurotoxicity if accidentally given intrathecally

monitoring: CBC with differential before each dose; observe WBC nadir (typically 5-10 days)
Injection site during and after administration for extravasation
Serum uric acid and renal function (tumour lysis risk)
counsel: This medicine is given only into a vein by trained staff and is dangerous by any other route
Report fever, sore throat, chills, or any sign of infection immediately (low white cells)
Report pain, burning, redness, or swelling at the injection site during or after treatment
Constipation is common - maintain fluids, fibre, and use prescribed laxatives
Use effective contraception; the drug can harm a developing baby and affect fertility
Report unusual bruising or bleeding, numbness, tingling, or breathing difficulty
pk: Antimitotic effect begins promptly after IV administration
Rapid distribution; WBC nadir at approximately 5-10 days post-dose
Triphasic; terminal elimination half-life approximately 25 hours
Myelosuppressive nadir lasts days; bone marrow usually recovers within 7-14 days
Store reconstituted/refrigerated at 2-8 C; protect from light
pearls: FOR INTRAVENOUS USE ONLY - intrathecal administration is uniformly fatal; always dispense with a warning overwrap/label
Vesicant - extravasation causes severe tissue injury; manage with heat and hyaluronidase
Dose-limiting toxicity is leukopenia (unlike vincristine, whose limit is neurotoxicity)
Reduce dose in hepatic impairment / hyperbilirubinemia
Acute pulmonary reactions can occur when combined with mitomycin-C
missed: Doses are administered in a clinic on a defined schedule. If a scheduled treatment is missed, contact the oncology team to reschedule; the next dose is adjusted based on the latest blood counts. Patients do not self-administer or make up doses.
overdose: Overdose produces exaggerated toxicity: profound myelosuppression, severe neurotoxicity (including features resembling vincristine toxicity), mucositis, and ileus. There is no specific antidote. Management is supportive: monitor blood counts for at least 3 weeks, give prophylactic antibiotics, blood products and growth factors as needed, prevent SIADH, and provide cardiovascular support. Some protocols use anticonvulsants and measures to limit neurotoxicity.
